transcript:
[00:00] Olivia Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Um, quick intro — I'm Olivia, AE at Redwood, with Samir our SE.
[00:07] Lena Vos: Hi all, Lena here, partnerships at Pegasus. Marco and Priya are with me.
[00:12] Marco Diaz: Hola, Marco from sales — nice to meet you.
[00:15] Samir Patel: Hey, good to meet you. We'll keep this light, want to learn about Pegasus and see alignment.
[00:22] Olivia Chen: Agenda — quick intros, how Pegasus thinks about partners, share a bit about Redwood offerings, then dig into infra and tech fit, and close with next steps. Sound good?
[00:32] Priya Sharma: Yep sounds good.
[00:34] Lena Vos: Perfect.
[02:01] Priya Sharma: Quick high level on Pegasus — we run GPU farms in NA and EU, mix of A100s, H100s, and some L40s in edge sites. We sell infra and partner with software vendors to provide turnkey inference stacks. Recently expanding partner program for inference runtimes.
[02:28] Marco Diaz: We're seeing demand from SaaS folks who want predictable inference costs and private deployments. They ask about VPC options and SSO — usual enterprise checklist.
[02:40] Olivia Chen: Great, that's right in our lane. Redwood provides Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private deploy (VPC/on-prem). For partners we do a couple of models: 1) referral/co-sell where you send customers to Redwood hosted; 2) dedicated joint offering where we run on your infra using Redwood Dedicated; 3) full Private deployment where Redwood software runs in your customer's VPC or on-prem with partner-managed infra.
[03:05] Lena Vos: For partner economics, which of those is easiest to enable?
[03:10] Samir Patel: Hosted referral is quickest — minimal integration. For deeper value it's Dedicated or Private. Dedicated requires us to map reserved capacity and throughput metrics; Private has more onboarding but higher ARR and better margin share.
[03:25] Priya Sharma: Technical question: how heavy is the runtime? Can it run on multi-tenant Pegasus clusters?
[03:32] Samir Patel: Good question. Redwood runtime is GPU-optimized but modular — it supports continuous batching, KV cache, and quantization-friendly paths. It can run on multi-tenant pools with containerization, but for predictable SLOs we often recommend dedicated pools or node-pinning. Note: sometimes the transcriber writes KV cache as KV cash, so ignore that.
[03:55] Marco Diaz: Regarding security — customers ask about KMS, audit logs, SOC2. Do you support customer-managed keys when Private deployed?
[04:02] Olivia Chen: Yes, Private supports KMS/HSM integration, and we ship audit logging and optional longer retention. For Dedicated we can provide customer-specific namespaces and audit hooks; hosted has RBAC and standard logging SAAS features.
[04:18] Lena Vos: Sounds good. Any certifications or compliance you can share?
[04:22] Samir Patel: We're SOC2 Type II and pursuing ISO 27001; we can share our security pack — will attach the security doc.
[04:30] Priya Sharma: On networking, does Redwood need outbound access for updates or callbacks? Some customers are air-gapped.
[04:37] Olivia Chen: For Private on-prem, we can do air-gapped installs. For VPC mode, minimal outbound for telemetry is optional; customers can opt-out and we support offline updates via signed bundles.
[04:50] Marco Diaz: Nice, that helps with regulated customers.
[06:05] Lena Vos: Let's dig into performance — customers compare latency/cost with NVIDIA NGC and other runtimes. What metrics should we benchmark?
[06:13] Samir Patel: We typically measure p99 latency, tokens/sec for streaming, throughput for batched workloads, and cost-per-1k-tokens given quantization. Also memory footprint and cold-start times. Would prefer a benchmark matrix with model families (LlamaX-ish, Mistral-like, GPT-family) and sequence lengths 64/256/1024.
[06:38] Priya Sharma: Do you support INT8/4 quantization and mixed precision?
[06:41] Samir Patel: Yes, we support a range of quantization profiles; sometimes specifics depend on the model and kernel support on the GPU. We'll note that kernel selection is automatic but we can provide recommended profiles per model.
[06:53] Marco Diaz: On the infra side, will we need NVLink or is PCIe fine?
[06:57] Samir Patel: For large model sharding NVLink helps; for single-GPU serving PCIe is fine. We can provide guidelines.
[07:12] Olivia Chen: Pricing — rough models are usage-based for hosted; committed capacity for Dedicated; and enterprise licensing for Private. For partner deals we typically do co-sell margins or reseller discounts. We'll share an example pricing sheet.
[07:30] Lena Vos: Good — partners want clarity on margins and deal registration.
[07:33] Olivia Chen: We'll include partner program terms in the deck.
[08:10] Priya Sharma: One technical item — what about model caching and hot-starts? If customers route requests across regions, does Redwood do prefix/KV caching to reduce tokens?
[08:20] Samir Patel: Yes, we do prefix and KV caching to reduce token generation, and we also do workload-aware batching to improve unit economics while keeping latency SLOs.
[08:31] Marco Diaz: Are there any limitations around model licenses or gated models?
[08:35] Olivia Chen: We surface a model catalog with verified performance and license status; for gated models we follow vendor licenses and can help customers manage that.
[09:02] Lena Vos: Any existing partners running Redwood on hosted or dedicated you can reference?
[09:07] Olivia Chen: We have a few early partners — some infra partners and SaaS platforms; we'll anonymize references but can provide case studies.
[10:00] Priya Sharma: For the technical deep dive, what data do you need from Pegasus to replicate performance?
[10:05] Samir Patel: Fleet inventory (GPU types, counts), region availability, typical network topology, expected workload profiles (latency-sensitive or batch), and whether customers prefer model variants. That will let us build a benchmark matrix.
[10:18] Lena Vos: We can export a CSV with fleet info and existing partner docs.
[10:22] Marco Diaz: Regarding SLAs — Redwood provides SLA for Dedicated?
[10:25] Olivia Chen: Yes, Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we can include SLOs in the partner agreement. Hosted has public SLAs as well.
[12:40] Priya Sharma: On observability — do you expose traces, token-level costs, and per-model dashboards?
[12:47] Samir Patel: Yes, Redwood Console includes token-level cost breakdowns, per-route/model dashboards, tracing hooks, and error analysis. We can add partner-level views to the console for joint customers.
[13:02] Lena Vos: How does routing/fallback work if Pegasus capacity is constrained?
[13:07] Samir Patel: We support smart routing policies — route by latency/cost/region/customer tier. We can also fallback to hosted or other model variants automatically if capacity runs low.
[13:20] Marco Diaz: That fallback is a big plus — customers want graceful degradation.
[15:00] Olivia Chen: Ok, quick recap: we'll send partner deck + pricing + security pack; Samir will propose benchmark plan and schedule the deep dive; Pegasus will send fleet matrix and partner docs. Any blockers?
[15:16] Priya Sharma: Not from our side. One note — some customers demand on-prem air-gapped installs; we'll want a quote for that.
[15:24] Olivia Chen: We'll include air-gap install options and a rough price range.
[15:40] Lena Vos: Also want clarity on partner onboarding timeline — how long to get a Private customer live?
[15:45] Samir Patel: Typical Private onboarding varies — small PoC few weeks, enterprise private tends to be 6–10 weeks depending on customer. We'll put a timeline in the runbook.
[17:02] Marco Diaz: Any legal items to pre-surface? Data residency, indemnity, and export controls typically come up.
[17:08] Olivia Chen: We'll include a partner legal checklist; our legal team can have a quick sync if needed.
[17:30] Priya Sharma: For the benchmark we prefer we run with 2–3 reference models and a mix of seq lengths, and run both latency and batch workload tests.
[17:40] Samir Patel: Sounds good. We'll propose the matrix and the scripts; we can run tests together or provide reproducible steps so Pegasus can run internally.
[18:05] Olivia Chen: Great. We'll also attach a short cheat-sheet on quantization profiles per GPU.
[18:20] Lena Vos: Awesome.
[18:25] Olivia Chen: Anything else?
[18:27] Marco Diaz: Not from me.
[18:30] Priya Sharma: No, that's it.
[18:32] Olivia Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the deck and scheduling links.
[18:38] Lena Vos: Thanks, bye.
[18:40] Meeting end: auto transcript notes may have minor mis-transcriptions (e.g., KV cache spelled as KV cash). Links shared: partner-deck.pdf (link), security-pack.pdf (link), benchmark-matrix-template.xlsx (link).
questions: Can Redwood run on Pegasus multi-tenant clusters or should partners use dedicated pools?
